content: Patients who have a known allergic reaction to penicillin should be advised to wear a medical identification tag or bracelet to alert healthcare providers in case of an emergency. Since most oral antibacterial drugs are optimally absorbed on an empty stomach, patients should be instructed to take penicillin one hour before meals or two hours after eating, unless otherwise directed by their physician. Patients must be informed to complete the entire prescribed course of therapy, even if symptoms such as fever or other signs of infection have resolved. This is critical to ensure the infection is fully treated and to prevent recurrence or resistance. If any of the following adverse reactions occur, patients should immediately discontinue the medication and contact their physician: shortness of breath, wheezing, skin rash, mouth irritation, black discoloration of the tongue, sore throat, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, swollen joints, or any unusual bleeding or bruising. Patients should not take any additional medications, including over-the-counter drugs such as antacids, laxatives, or vitamins, without prior approval from their physician. Patients should be counseled that antibacterial drugs, including dicloxacillin sodium capsules, are intended solely for the treatment of bacterial infections. These medications are not effective against viral infections, such as the common cold. When prescribed dicloxacillin sodium capsules for a bacterial infection, patients should be informed that while they may feel better early in the course of therapy, it is essential to take the medication exactly as directed. Skipping doses or failing to complete the full course of therapy can reduce the effectiveness of the treatment and increase the risk of bacterial resistance, making future infections more difficult to treat with dicloxacillin or other antibacterial drugs. Diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotics and typically resolves once the antibiotic is discontinued. However, patients should be made aware that watery and bloody stools, with or without stomach cramps and fever, can occur even two or more months after completing the antibiotic course. If this happens, they should contact their physician immediately. The interaction between alcohol and dicloxacillin has not been established. Patients should consult their doctor regarding the potential effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication. Dicloxacillin is marketed under the brand name Dynapen®. There is limited information available regarding look-alike drug names for dicloxacillin in the drug labeling.
